html:
Muay Thai is the Thai art of kickboxing, using fists, elbows, knees and shins. In the 1920s and 1930s it took its modern form, with gloves, a ring, timed rounds and weight classes.

It grew from old fighting skills of Siamese soldiers. Thai tradition tells of Nai Khanom Tom, a fighter captured at the fall of Ayutthaya, who won his freedom by beating Burmese boxers.

Bouts at Bangkok's Lumpinee and Rajadamnern stadiums, with music and a ritual dance before each fight, became a national passion. From the 1990s gyms spread worldwide, and it became a core of mixed martial arts. See Bangkok and Thailand.
